vehicle: Ford Kuga Mk2 2.0 TDCi (2012-2019, incl. Focus Mk3 / C-Max platform relatives)
disclaimer: Community-sourced known issues. 'known_issue: yes' means widely documented across owner forums and specialist repairers — it is NOT a guarantee your car has this fault. Verify with diagnostics before buying parts. Contribute corrections via pull request with a source link.

issues.title: DPF differential pressure sensor hoses / wiring failure
likely_causes: Split or chafed rubber hoses between sensor and DPF pipes (most common)
Soot-blocked metal take-off pipe nipple on the exhaust
Broken conductor inside the loom near the sensor plug (often blue wire with tracer)
Failed differential pressure sensor (only after the above are excluded)
Genuinely soot/ash-loaded DPF
checks: Read live DPF differential pressure: ~0-3 kPa at idle is healthy
Inspect both hoses end-to-end; blow through metal nipples
Continuity-test loom wires, do not trust visual inspection
fixes: FORScan: reset DPF + sensor learned values

issues.title: Powershift 6DCT450 (wet-clutch auto) harsh/scratching shifts 1-2-3
likely_causes: Mechatronic valve body / hydraulic pressure loss (most documented)
Clutch pack wear (internal spring system collapse)
Debris blocking mechatronic oil pathways
TCU software calibration (reflash can improve shift quality)
Degraded/incorrect transmission fluid
checks: Read TCM codes (module 7E1) - not visible on the dashboard
Check fluid condition and level procedure (temperature-dependent)
Note whether symptoms are worse cold (hydraulic/mechatronic) or hot (clutch)
fixes: Clutch kit (specialist rebuild, ~£1,000-2,500 in UK references)

issues.title: AWD (Haldex-type coupling) pump failure with NO dashboard warning
symptoms: front wheels spin in slippery conditions
likely_causes: Failed AWD pre-charge pump at the rear differential (filter gauze clogged from missed coupling oil services)
DEM (AWD control module) internal failure
Broken earth strap / blown fuse / corroded connector at the pump
Coupling oil never changed (service item often skipped)
checks: Scan the DEM module directly - dash shows nothing; codes like P1889 sit in the module only
Check pump fuse and earth strap before condemning parts
DEM is often on the MS-CAN bus - adapter needs an HS/MS-CAN switch to see it
fixes: Pump + filter kit (e.g. OE 8V41-4C019-AA family) - NOTE: new pump requires a learn procedure via diagnostics

issues.title: Coolant / water contamination in engine oil
likely_causes: Oil cooler seal/housing failure (O-ring goes brittle, housing cracks at the seal seat - documented on this engine family)
EGR cooler internal failure (coolant loss with bubbles in expansion tank)
Head gasket (specialists report it is RARE on this engine - suspect it last)
Water pump / timing cover seepage (external, not mixing)
checks: Oil cooler off and inspect seal seat for cracks before anything else (cheapest, most likely)
Bubbles in expansion tank while running = EGR cooler or combustion gas path
Coolant system pressure test
fixes: Head gasket only after both coolers excluded

issues.title: PCM loses adaptations / settings after battery replacement
likely_causes: BMS (battery monitoring) not reset after new battery - charging logic wrong
Voltage dip during replacement corrupted a marginal EEPROM/flash cell
Failing PCM flash memory exposed by the power cycle
checks: Manual BMS reset (high beams x5, brake x3 within 10s, battery lamp flashes x3)
Idle/throttle relearn drive cycle
If codes persist after correct resets: PCM bench test (see docs/PCM_REPLACEMENT_GUIDE.md)

issues.title: EGR valve / intake carbon clogging
likely_causes: Carbon buildup on EGR valve and intake swirl flaps
Short-journey driving pattern
checks: Live EGR position vs commanded
Intake inspection
sources: community-reported; source link welcome via PR

issues.title: Injector seal failure ('chuffing') and carbon buildup around injectors
likely_causes: Copper injector washer/seal failure
Injector clamp loosening
checks: Visual around each injector with engine running
Listen for chuff at idle
sources: community-reported; source link welcome via PR

issues.title: Dual-mass flywheel rattle / judder
symptoms: rattle at idle that disappears with clutch pressed
likely_causes: DMF wear (age/mileage)
Aggressive clutch use / towing
checks: Rattle test at idle with clutch in/out
Specialist free-play check
sources: community-reported; source link welcome via PR
